speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When I spoke in March 2020, we were seeing the centre of the pandemic shift away from China, and a rapid increase in cases globally.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Close to 80% of our cases then were imported, mainly from returning Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We tightened our border controls and our import cases have drastically reduced.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the past week, we had no imported cases, down from around 16 a day on average in March.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are signs that our circuit breaker measures are working.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The average number of new unlinked community cases a day had similarly reduced from 12, to five over the same period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This suggests that our circuit breaker measures are effective.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It has not been easy, but you have all played a part in bringing these numbers down and I want to express my heartfelt gratitude.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we are not out of the woods yet.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While the community cases are coming under control, we have seen a rise in migrant worker cases, particularly in the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We moved in quickly, set up medical posts in all the purpose-built dormitories and provided mobile medical support for the factory converted dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH worked with the Inter-agency Task Force led by MOM to ensure the medical needs and welfare of the workers are taken care of.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are grateful for the assistance of the Task Force's members including the SAF and SPF and our healthcare workers from our public healthcare institutions as well as from the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are making progress and will continue to do our best to care for our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Teo will elaborate on this in her Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Notwithstanding stringent precautions, there have also been cases at our Nursing Homes and at one Welfare Home.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As these facilities serve the elderlies who are a vulnerable group, we take such cases very seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has ramped up more aggressive testing for staff and residents at these Homes, working jointly with MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is to protect our vulnerable seniors, by quickly picking up hidden cases if any, to isolate them and care for them and thus protect the rest of the Homes' residents and staff.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have started this, but it would take some time to complete.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Meanwhile, we may see cases picked up at these Homes as a result of the active screening.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, we are also arranging lodging for staff who interact with residents at designated accommodation facilities on-site or at hotels, to reduce their exposure to the community during this circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Both these steps complement existing safe distancing and infection control measures, so as to enhance protection to our seniors in these Homes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Overall, despite our high case numbers, we have managed to keep death rates low so far.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is partly because most of our patients are younger and partly due to the tireless efforts of our healthcare workers in providing good and timely medical care for all our COVID-infected patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must continue to do all we can to save patients who become gravely ill and keep fatalities as low as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In preparation for the expected increase in the number of cases, especially from the dormitories, we have rapidly expanded our healthcare capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This includes both medical facilities, and also healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have seen countries whose healthcare systems were overwhelmed and this quickly led to high numbers of death among patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Irene Quay has asked if we have an ethical framework to allocate use of healthcare resources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are working hard to avoid getting to this point.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have planned ahead, created and ramped up many different types of healthcare facilities to support the specific needs of COVID-19 patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, our healthcare system has the flexibility to stretch our capacity to respond to increasing demand.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To ensure that there is available hospital capacity to care for COVID-19 patients, public hospitals have postponed non-urgent elective procedures and discharged medically stable long-stayers to step-down care facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Public hospitals have also repurposed and converted existing wards into isolation rooms and progressively opened more wards for COVID-19 patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NCID has also increased their capacity from about 100 to more than 500 negative pressure isolation beds in the same period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Currently, 28 COVID-19 patients are in our ICU, as the majority of the cases are mild.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have about 150 vacant ICU beds and can quickly bring another 300 online.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we are not taking any chances as we must preserve our buffer capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Leon Perera had asked about our ability to further ramp up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also ensured a sufficient supply of ventilators and other ICU accessories to support the care of ICU patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The majority of our COVID-19 cases have only mild symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Hence, we have expanded our medical facilities to care for patients with mild symptoms and those who are on the recovery path and no longer need extensive medical support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These facilities allow the hospitals to focus resources on providing care to those who require emergency and intensive care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Community Care Facility (CCF) is one such facility for patients with milder symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the CCFs, patients continue to be monitored and have access to appropriate medical care when needed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include places such as the D'Resort at Paris Ris, Singapore Expo Halls 1 to 6 and part of Changi Exhibition Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Building up our CCF capacity called for a multi-agency effort comprising Government agencies and the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many teams had worked round the clock to make this possible, and I want to extend my gratitude to all of them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, for the first hall in Expo, this was made possible through the hard work of individuals from Temasek Holdings, Singapore Expo, Surbana Jurong, the Integrated Health Information Systems, Resorts World Sentosa as the managing agent, PSA, ST Engineering, Certis Cisco, Parkway Pantai and the Woodlands Health Campus as well as the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The list is long, but this gives us a sense of the complexity of the operations and how closely everyone had to work together.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through the efforts of everyone involved, we managed to set up the first hall in a week.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is truly an exemplary example of a Whole-of-Society effort.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Next, let me talk about Community Recovery Facility (CRF).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also set up these CRFs which is a step-down facility for recovering patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Based on epidemiological evidence and research by local and international infectious disease experts, patients who remain well at day 14 of their illness are past the critical stage and are unlikely to need further medical care.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, they still have to be isolated to reduce the risk of transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As our CRF facilities increase, we can also free up space at the CCFs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With this layered set of healthcare facilities customised to patient needs, we will be able to provide the most appropriate care for patients while also ensuring sufficient healthcare capacity to meet our needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All these efforts require close coordination among multiple agencies, as the example of CCF @ Singapore Expo illustrates, to ensure operations are optimised, facilities are well-managed, patient flows are facilitated and tracked, while keeping watch on the capacity utilisation overall.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has set up a Medical Operations Task Force (MOTF) with the support of the SAF to oversee and coordinate our efforts on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I want to thank our partners and SAF in particular, for their support and efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Looking ahead, while we take heart in the progress made, especially in the community cases, we should not be complacent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are still unlinked cases and cases picked up from our surveillance programme, indicating the presence of hidden cases in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Globally, the number of cases also continue to increase.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even countries and regions with low daily numbers, such as China, Hong Kong, South Korea and New Zealand, are watching out anxiously for a second wave of infection that may result in another prolonged outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Hence, we must continue to do what we can to keep our cases low, to keep the lid tight even as we gradually roll back some of our circuit breaker measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are now at the end of the two weeks of tighter circuit breaker measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Last Saturday, the Multi-Ministry Task Force announced the gradual resumption of selected activities and services in the coming weeks, subject to the necessary safe management measures being in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we work together, by 1 June, we hope our situation would have improved further, with community cases remaining low or coming down further.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Migrant worker cases in the dormitories will hopefully by then be clearly under control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is important to enable our people to start going back to work.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is also important for Singapore to protect our strategic position in the global supply chains as the global economy recovers from COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will still need to open up in a phased and calibrated manner, to avoid a second wave of outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There will likely still be cases of infection in the community as the virus is difficult to eradicate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: What is key is to keep the number of cases small and reduce the risk of big clusters, through various safeguards and enablers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It would take a while before the COVID-19 outbreak subsides globally or before a vaccine is available.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Thus, we will have to adapt to a new way of life and social interactions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked what indicators we will look at in considering lifting the circuit breaker measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, numbers are important but they are not the only thing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We need to be assured that community transmission locally is stemmed or very low.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also need to see a decrease in migrant worker cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These cases are high today partly due to proactive case-finding in some settings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we have been able to keep local community cases low despite higher number of cases among migrant workers, it is equally important to reduce the migrant worker cases over time, though it will take a while longer.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Otherwise, we will continue to be at risk of a spillover from the dormitories into the wider population.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we need to make an assessment of the situation globally and for individual countries to inform the extent and approach on reopening our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will review the rate of transmissions in other countries as well as what they have done to contain the spread.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For any reopening of our borders, we are likely to start small and selectively, and to continue to impose a mix of isolation and test requirements to protect ourselves from new imported cases leading to community spread.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, we must put in place a system to allow us to open up safely.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When we allow more business and social activities to resume, there will be more interactions and higher risks of virus transmission at the workplace and in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, we need to step up our capability and capacity to test and detect cases early, contact trace quickly, ringfence close contacts promptly and establish the original source of the infection to stop other undetected transmission chains, if any.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These are the key enablers which will give us confidence to reopen.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is among the highest testing rates in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we plan to do more and will continue to expand our testing capacity and to strategically deploy them to yield the greatest impact.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members have asked about different tests and their uses.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Today, we use mainly the polymerase chain reaction, or PCR tests, to detect confirmed COVID-19 cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The PCR works by detecting the virus RNA from a nose or throat swab and is the gold standard for detecting current infection.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To the question by Ms Sylvia Lim, we use PCR testing for three key purposes: (a) to diagnose suspect cases to provide early treatment and isolate close contacts; (b) to do screening and active case finding of individuals at risk, such as migrant workers decanted from their dorms before they return to work; and (c) to do surveillance to monitor undetected cases in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With this increase, we will widen the net that we cast for diagnostic testing for symptomatic cases, active case finding, screening and surveillance testing in our community and among workers, including migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also do more testing and monitoring to pick out asymptomatic and pre-symptomatic cases among priority groups such as nursing home residents and staff to prevent clusters from developing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Testing is crucial as risk of infection will increase when we allow more economic and social activities to resume.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Ms Foo Mee Har had asked about another type of test called serology testing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This works by detecting antibodies produced by the body to fight against the virus from a blood sample.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Based on our local studies, the effectiveness of such tests is very low in the first 10 days of illness as it takes time for the immune system to develop antibodies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, unlike the PCR testing, serology tests are useful to indicate past infection but it is not very useful for early diagnosis because of the time lag.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many such tests in the market are also still under review and validation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Notwithstanding this, NCID has begun to use serology testing to study the level of infection among various groups, including healthcare workers, close contacts of COVID-19 patients and the general population.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This shows that the infection rate among our healthcare workers and general population is low.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: That means they had been infected earlier but recovered, and remain well without any symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This points to the need to continue our efforts to quickly isolate close contacts of confirmed cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will continue to do more of these studies to help us understand the extent of spread and immunity in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I should add that scientific evidence of protective immunity is still under intensive study currently.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There have been some suggestions to do asymptomatic testing for the entire population.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As there is no widespread community transmission here, the yield will be very low if asymptomatic testing is done indiscriminately for the whole population.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To be effective, it may also need to be done repeatedly as it does not reflect immunity and those tested can be infected after the test.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It might not be best way to use our testing resources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, we will and have started doing asymptomatic testing selectively for priority groups.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, we currently test asymptomatic young children if they are in the same household as COVID-19 patients since they may not be able to articulate their symptoms well.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, a key priority is to protect vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such tests complement existing precautionary measures, such as good infection control practices and close monitoring for symptoms in staff and residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They will allow us to intervene early where needed to protect the elderly residents.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As more businesses reopen, we may also do more tests for essential service workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At our borders, we can also deploy tests for arrivals to reduce the risk of local transmission from imported cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In all, as we build up our testing capacity, we will be able to test more and for more purposes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be important as we start to open up so that we can pre-emptively detect and break any potential transmission chains.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The second enabler is our contact tracing capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: After we have confirmed a COVID-19 case, we will need to contact trace and isolate high-risk close contacts to limit the spread in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This needs to be done fast and has to be scalable and thorough for it to be effective.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we must scale up quickly if there are more cases or large clusters and to discover less obvious links.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To do so manually will be very difficult.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many countries have leveraged on technology to help them contact trace effectively and efficiently.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also explore how we can tap on SafeEntry and TraceTogether as well as other technological solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we build our capability and capacity for testing, contact tracing and healthcare infrastructure, we need the support of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They are at the centre of our fight against this COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We deeply appreciate their sacrifices, long hours as well as personal and professional commitment to care for each patient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This will be a long campaign and we will need the support of our healthcare workers, and we need to support them and to take care of their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many Members of Parliament have asked about the well-being of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our key priority is in keeping them safe and healthy by ensuring adequate supply of personal protective equipment to protect our healthcare workers and provide them training on the proper usage.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Based on investigations thus far, there are no established epidemiological links of a healthcare worker being infected in the line of duty for caring for their patients, except for one case in a private healthcare institution where we are unable to rule out the possible link between the doctor and a COVID-19 patient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our healthcare workers have taken an extra level of care at their workplace to protect themselves and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The recent NCID study also did not detect any past infection among a sample of healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have reminded our healthcare workers constantly that they should take adequate precautions during their work to protect themselves, the patients as well as their family members.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the event that our healthcare workers fall sick, we will ensure that they are well taken care of and our healthcare institutions will provide them with the necessary support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is also important for us to take care of the mental well-being of our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even before the COVID-19 pandemic, the healthcare clusters had measures in place, such as counselling clinics, helplines and peer support programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, our institutions have rostered breaks and staff rotations to ensure that healthcare workers have sufficient rest periods in between work days.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The clusters have also been actively working with the NTUC and, in particular, the Healthcare Services Employees' Union (HSEU) with initiatives such as the distribution of care packages, the launch of GrabCare to provide transport for our frontline workers and collaboration with MindFi, a mindfulness app.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The many gifts and words of encouragement from members of the public to our healthcare workers mean a lot to them and have helped to keep up their morale.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members of the public have been writing thank you messages and buying breakfast for our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As part of the SG United initiative, close to 9,000 messages for our healthcare workers were collected from appreciation zones across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On behalf of our healthcare workers, let me thank you for your continued support.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Compensation is another important area, which Miss Cheryl Chan asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We recognise the invaluable contributions of our workers and will ensure that they receive due recognition for stepping up during this challenging period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Healthcare workers are also paid shift or overtime allowances if they take on longer or more shifts during this outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, we recognise that no monetary compensation is ever enough.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I want to again acknowledge and thank our healthcare workers for their hard work and dedication.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: One great example is Ms Tovelle Loh, an assistant nurse clinician from NCID.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Ms Loh supports training of staff to ensure that they are updated on infection control policies and recommendations and also helps to review infection control workflows at NCID and other settings.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite the heavy work load, she remains spirited and committed to do the best for her patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And it helps that her husband has been very supportive.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Examples like Ms Loh abound, among our frontline workers, support staff and also researchers in our testing and research labs.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Another key part of our strategy is to augment the healthcare workforce, which Mr Murali Pillai had asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While our public healthcare sector currently has sufficient healthcare professionals, they are stretched, and there is a need to rotate and refresh staff periodically, as the fight against COVID-19 is likely to be a long one.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have expanded the scope to include those without prior healthcare experience, for whom training will be provided to enable them to take on supporting roles, such as performing swab procedures and basic care roles.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Members of the SG Healthcare Corps will be remunerated for their time and contribution when they are deployed to work alongside our healthcare workers on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, we also use technology as a force multiplier, to deliver the same or enhanced outcomes, with less time and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, in the CCFs, round-the-clock care is made possible through the use of medical kiosks and teleconsultations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Devices such as pulse oximeters and health apps are also used to monitor patient well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Healthcare institutions have also started teleconsultation services for follow-ups on their patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through all these initiatives, we aim to ensure that our public healthcare services remain available to those in need, and our healthcare workers are well taken care of during this challenging period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This enables us to have a sustainable healthcare workforce in this long-term fight.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as we fight COVID-19, we need to continue to address long-term health issues.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am glad that Prof Lim Sun Sun asked about this, and let me share what we have been doing in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have temporarily deferred launching any new initiatives to allow staff to be re-deployed to more critical areas of COVID-19 work.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But for selected programmes, such as measures on Sugar Sweetened Beverages, banning Partially-hydrogenated Oils, and standardised packaging for tobacco products, we will continue to push ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To support our safe distancing measures, we have already suspended all on-ground activities such as general health screening, but we will continue to encourage Singapore residents to practice healthy habits and fight diabetes through less resource-intensive alternative platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, HPB continues to provide on HealthHub, bite-sized videos and articles on practising good personal hygiene, healthy eating, physical activity, and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We must also never let our guard down on dengue.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With the traditional dengue peak season approaching, NEA officers are on the ground conducting dengue inspections at common areas and construction sites, where construction site operators continue to be responsible for vector control measures, even during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A worrying trend that NEA observed was a 50% increase in Aedes mosquito breeding in homes over the past three years, compared to the preceding three years.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Masagos has asked me to urge everyone at home to be vigilant, to do the Mozzie Wipeout to remove potential mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NEA also brought forward the National Dengue Prevention campaign to 22 March to rally all members of the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our efforts on all these fronts continue even as we battle the COVID-19 outbreak, to keep Singaporeans healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In this fight against the COVID-19 pandemic, everyone can play a role, during and after the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We acknowledge that the circuit breaker measures are difficult, and we appreciate everyone's support and sacrifice to stay home and adhere to the measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For our frontline officers, including those in healthcare, and dorm operations, we stand behind you, and want to express our enormous gratitude for your efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our collective efforts are not in vain, and we have seen a decrease in our community numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are looking ahead, and making preparations for post 1 June.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we all do our part, we can overcome and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Let us work together and move forward together, as one SG United.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, over the past month, our battle against COVID-19 has escalated sharply.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, we have ramped up our resources significantly in response to the challenges, and today, we are continuing to fight the virus on two main fronts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have had a huge spike in cases at the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The infection is mostly concentrated amongst workers in the construction sector.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We now know that the transmission amongst this group has been happening for some time, and occurred not just in the dormitories, but also in common worksites and in places that they went to with their friends after work and on their rest days.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we had clusters outside of the dormitories too – amongst construction workers living in shophouses and private apartments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To determine the extent of the spread, we have undertaken extensive testing amongst these workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of the workers have very mild symptoms and they sometimes brush this aside as a very mild cold.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we are testing not just the workers who report sick, but also those that are asymptomatic and well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This intensive testing explains the large numbers that we are still picking up amongst migrant workers in the dormitories, and we expect this to continue for a few more weeks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we have implemented a comprehensive set of support measures to look after the health, well-being and welfare of these workers, which Minister Josephine Teo will elaborate on later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are very mindful of our responsibility to these migrant workers who have contributed so much to Singapore, and we will continue to ensure that they get the care and support they need.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know the restrictions have not been easy and have created considerable inconveniences.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But Singaporeans have been resilient and have taken all these in your stride.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For this, we want to thank everyone for doing their part.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I must strongly caution that the easing of some measures in the coming weeks cannot be taken as a signal that we can now take it easy and start to go out more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This battle against the virus is not a sprint; it is a marathon, and we are not even at the halfway mark!

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if you have done a marathon, you will know that the second half is typically harder than the first.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must stay vigilant, maintain our discipline, continue to stay home and minimise our contacts with others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we continue this fight against the virus, we also learn more about how the virus is transmitted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we update our risk assessments and adjust our measures accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And as I said just now, we must expect more challenges along this journey, which may require us to take further adjustments in our measures or to take additional precautions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For members of the public, I can appreciate that it is sometimes difficult to keep up with all the changes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I hope that everyone appreciates and understands that we are responding to a dynamic and fast changing situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In every case, we will carefully consider the latest scientific evidence and medical advice and the impact on our people before making a change.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our overriding objective has always been and will continue to be the health and well-being of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, at the start of the outbreak, we had to implement many new travel restrictions and adjust them quickly as we tracked how the virus was spreading from country to country.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Later, in coming up with specific measures for our community, we too had to adapt and adjust as we learnt more about the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has happened not just in Singapore, but everywhere around the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are dealing with a new virus, and scientists everywhere are discovering more about the virus, even today, and the disease it causes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Prof Leo Yee Sin, Executive Director of NCID has said, "for us to be ahead of the virus... we   know the enemy very well", and right now, "we're still on the learning curve".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is not just Singapore which is on the learning curve, the whole world is still on the learning curve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we updated our guidance on masks as we learnt more about the virus, and then we made it a requirement for everyone to wear masks when they go out.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also explained then, that the wearing of mask is not the only, nor the most important protective measure.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Remember that the virus can spread through surfaces as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the wearing of masks must be complemented with other precautions that we have emphasised from the outset, including safe distancing and good personal hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked if we should make it compulsory to wear masks when you are out in all circumstances; even when ones engages in strenuous exercise outside.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Actually, the issue here is not just about the wearing of masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The more fundamental issue is whether we want to allow people to go outside to exercise in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Going out for exercise is beneficial for your immunity and health.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a risk of transmission only if you are in close contact with another person for some time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if you exercise alone in the open with safe distancing, as you are required to, this should not pose a problem.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is also no local evidence of transmission occurring among people exercising in the open.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a balance which other countries have struck too – take the example of the Czech Republic.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I mentioned this because there was a video going around earlier on how they were amongst the first European countries to impose a requirement for people to wear masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the Czech Republic today, you can go out to exercise and you do not need to wear a mask, so long as you maintain a safe distance from others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some think we do not need to bother with these very careful calibrations and just go for a "full lockdown".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if you look at the countries on lockdowns, the measures they implement are not the same, even if they use the same term.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is more important is to understand the specific measures that are needed in our own context and circumstance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, one of the most effective ways to slow down the spread of the virus is to restrict movement altogether, get everyone to just stay home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung puts it – he coined a very catchy phrases to explain this to the elderly in Mandarin: "如果你不出门, 你就不会见人; 如果你不见人, 病毒就不会进门".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In translation, "If you don't go out, you won't meet people; if you don't meet people, you won't bring the virus home." It does not have the same ring in English but you get the point.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Staying home can be an effective measure but keeping everyone at home also has substantial social and economic costs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The impact is likely to be felt disproportionately by the lower income and the vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are also less likely to be able to telecommute for work so staying home will clearly affect their incomes and livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It was a difficult decision to make because we knew businesses and workers are already hurting.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in the end, we decided we had to proceed with this move, so as to break the transmission chain and slow down the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For all Singaporeans, we have the Solidarity payment of $600, with more support for those with children and other support, such as the COVID-19 Support Grant and the Temporary Relief Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking ahead, as we think about easing some of the circuit breaker measures, we will adopt this same evidence-based approach to assess the transmission risks, and then make careful and calibrated adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, no shuttling to and fro but you move one time and you stay there.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there will also be many requests we have to reject.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are already getting appeals for more relaxation for more businesses to open, for my favourite shop to open.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And you can guess which one is top on the list, going beyond what we have announced.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have to hold the line for now and I hope Singaporeans understand why we need to be firm and why everyone must do their part to cooperate and comply with these measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members – Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Ms Anthea Ong – had asked for a review and inquiry into the cause of the outbreak in the dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do want to continue taking feedback and suggestions to improve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is our basic attitude – to keep improving, learning and doing better.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we are now still in the heat of battle.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When all this is over, we will certainly look back and learn from the experience.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We do that each time, after a crisis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, our lessons from SARS have helped us a lot in dealing with COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, at the right time, we will comprehensively review this pandemic and our responses – not just the outbreak in the dormitories, but the entire crisis from start to finish, and our overall response, and we will seek to learn and improve.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I have no doubt that we will find many things where we could have done better and many changes we should make to be better prepared the next time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for now, let us stay focused on the urgent priorities ahead of us – we have to bring the outbreak under control on the two fronts, in the community and in the migrant worker dormitories, so that we may then resume activities gradually.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And indeed, looking ahead, the key challenge for us and for countries everywhere, is to work out how we can exit from the circuit breaker and resume normal activities safely, without the virus flaring up again.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Easing on the measures prematurely and without proper safeguards can result in a second wave of transmission and then force a second round of tightening, which I am sure no one wants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has happened in other countries and it reinforces the need for us to move cautiously.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we take these steps to resume activities, there will be major challenges to tackle.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A construction worksite will typically have hundreds of workers coming from multiple dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One single infected worker – mild or asymptomatic – can spread the virus to their co-workers at the worksite.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They in turn can bring the infection back to where they live and also to places they gather with their friends.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When that happens, large clusters will quickly form, as has happened.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How do we avoid this from happening again?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to work with the industry to fundamentally change the way we go about construction activities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will need a whole range of measures covering the worksites, the accommodation and transport of workers, as well as additional precautions taken by the workers themselves.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this applies to all sectors of the economy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All firms will need to change their work culture and practices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Life after the circuit breaker will not be a return to status quo ante.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why MTI and MOM are engaging industry associations, business chambers and firms, to help them adapt to these new realities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There will need to be split team arrangements with no cross-deployment of staff, staggered working and lunch break hours, higher hygiene standards, amongst a whole range of different measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within the workplace, there should not be any gathering of staff in groups at any time, be it in the pantry or the staff canteen.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Very simple measures, but every company has to take them seriously.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Wherever possible, we should make full use of technology to enable the implementation of these measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And all of these safeguards must be in place before we can allow workplaces to re-open more and allow more people to resume going to work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I do not think we can restart these activities anytime soon.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, it may take some time for us to allow dining in at F&B outlets.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand many people are looking forward to doing that with their family members and friends, but we will have to assess the risks and consider this very carefully, considering that this particular activity is a known vector for transmission.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Religious gatherings and services too may take a while to resume.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, all our communities have experienced or will be experiencing their religious observances and holidays under very different circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From Qing Ming and Easter in April, and soon Vesak Day and Hari Raya in May.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know it has not been easy and we really appreciate everyone's understanding of the adjustments that have to be made to keep ourselves and our families safe during this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And to open up safely, we will need to do two other things which Minister Gan highlighted just now – to ramp up testing and to harness technology for faster contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A nation-wide testing strategy is being developed, even as we scale up testing capacity, as shared by Minister Gan earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And then, we will progressively expand testing to the rest of the essential workforce and the broader community, in line with the expansion of our testing capacity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the technology front, we have implemented two key tools.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The first is SafeEntry, which is a digital check-in/check-out system to log the visits by individuals in all business premises and venues.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The second is a TraceTogether app, which uses Bluetooth on your phones to quickly identify whom you have been near to, so that we can track your close contacts when the need arises.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The team is now working with Apple and Google to enhance this app and to make it more effective, especially on iOS phones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, we are also developing solutions for the elderly and young who may not have smartphones.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, that is also a group we are focusing on.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And there is a whole series of work around the technology front.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When the work is ready, we will announce more details.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they are not a substitute for personal responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of us still have to play a part, by practising good personal hygiene habits, wearing a mask when we are outside and seeking medical attention immediately when we are unwell.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The entire team has been working flat out over this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They include our healthcare workers; contact tracers and infectious disease experts; researchers, scientists and lab technicians; our communications team who help to put out accurate and timely information; our safe distancing ambassadors and enforcement officers deployed all over Singapore; our officers manning our checkpoints, isolation and quarantine facilities; the SAF, SPF, SCDF officers mobilised across different areas; and public officers from all Ministries working hard to support the overall effort – they are mobilising volunteers, securing more spaces for the different needs we have, helping with relief measures and mask distribution – a whole range of work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Co-Chair of the Task Force, I get a front row seat in seeing the best of Singapore at work during this crisis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this has been truly a humbling and inspiring experience, because everywhere I go, I see people who are tired but they remain fully committed and focused on the mission and they are still going all out to get the job done.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some have had to quickly adapt to the new requirements of working from home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Like our teachers who have been busy designing new curriculum and engaging students on home-based learning; and they are now getting ready for the first batch of students returning to schools in two weeks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For others, it has been a complete change in their job scope.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Ms Jaime Lim, who is a Deputy Director at MOM said, and I quote, "My work went from being desk-bound to manning safe distancing measures ops command and now I am at a dormitory gazetted as an isolation area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Stationed at the dormitory, weekends and weekdays have merged into a blur.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am now used to foggy face shields, powdery palms from glove wear and facial marks made by masks".

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many others, like Jaime, have gone above and beyond the call of duty.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, a big "Thank You" goes out to everyone on the frontline.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are working their guts out, taking care of fellow Singaporeans, fighting the virus and controlling the outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also deeply appreciate all who are in essential services, who have kept Singapore going through this circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They include our cleaners, facilities managers, technicians, refuse collectors, workers in the power and water industries, public transport workers, social service professionals, security guards, delivery riders, taxi drivers and so many more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also very heartening to see many ground-up initiatives from community groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many social service organisations are helping the more vulnerable groups cope with the circuit breaker and providing additional support to our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Thousands of volunteers have signed up for initiatives ranging from mask distribution, helping with applications for Temporary Relief Funds and appreciating our frontline workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, to everyone out there working during the circuit breaker, to those working from home and to those supporting the fight in whatever way you can, we also want to say “Thank You” for your contributions and sacrifices.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are all on the frontline in this fight against the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every contribution counts and helps in our overall efforts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These examples show us how much more effective we can all be when we stand together and combine our efforts across the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will leave in its wake a permanently changed world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Uncertainly and instability may rise in some countries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore will endeavour to be in this group.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To do so, all of us must continue to work together and support each other.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the time for us to stand as one nation – to beat the virus, overcome the crisis and emerge stronger together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM has been supporting the fight on the economic front and also on the public health front.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our priority is to protect the livelihoods of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That remains so even as a new battlefront emerged.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Equally important now is to take care of our migrant workers' health.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In my statement today, I will cover both aspects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last week, I updated the public on the labour market situation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, in the first quarter of the year, the full impact of COVID-19 was not yet felt.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the impact was not even; foreign employment fell significantly while local employment still managed some growth.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are signs that employers are trying hard to cut costs to save jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They, too, want businesses to restart quickly when conditions allow.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are being helped by the significant wage support through the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, as well as the tripartite consensus on managing excess manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Later this month, more than $4 billion will be paid out additionally.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government provided levy waivers and rebates to help employers meet their obligations to their foreign employees during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another $675 million is expected to be paid out by July.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides support for their employers, we are providing more direct support for our lower wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many of them are in essential services and are continuing to work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They will get enhanced Workfare payouts which took effect in January, of up to $4,000 annually.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will be in two tranches – in July and October.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Total Workfare payouts this year will be about $2.2 billion.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Inevitably, even with Government support, troubles with business can strain labour relations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In dealing with the disputes, the tripartite partners agree to uphold the principles of fairness and shared responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not all employers have been impacted to the same degree.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those in better shape financially should use all the Government support to provide their employees with a more generous baseline wage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others who are financially stressed and face poor business prospects should be frank with their unions and employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They should work out together how to use the Government support to help each other get through this period of difficulty.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One thing is clear: employers should not act unilaterally and put their employees on prolonged no-pay leave or reduced pay without the employees' consent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Mr Dennis Tan’s question, employees who need help can approach the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management for advisory and mediation services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The National Wages Council also issued a helpful set of guidelines in March.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, it encouraged companies to use any lull in their business to train their workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SkillsFuture Singapore has an Enhanced Training Support Package that covers up to 90% of course fees for employers in selected sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many courses come with absentee payroll that give employers in all sectors extra wage support – 90% of the hourly basic salary, up to $10 an hour.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit of $10,000 further helps employers pay for up to 90% of out-of-pocket expenses that are not already subsidised by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SIRS scheme was designed and implemented in record time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who qualify need not apply and are instead automatically included.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We know, as a result, that there may be deserving SEPs who should also be considered.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We, therefore, appreciate NTUC for stepping forward to help with the appeals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More than that, NTUC is helping through the SEP Training Support Scheme (STSS) which now provides an hourly training allowance of $10.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This comes to about $400 for a week-long course.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While modest compared to the income SEPs may have earned in the past, it will still help defray their daily expenditure as they learn new skills during this downtime.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am very encouraged that already, about 1,800 SEPs will benefit from the scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One of them is 34-year-old Jovan, who has been a freelance band director for MOE schools for the past 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since the suspension of CCA programmes, Jovan has made good use of time freed up and attended seven different courses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They include SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace, Setting up and Running a Business and How to Pitch Like a Pro, all of which he finds useful.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whether for SEPs or regular employees, finding a job at such times will not be easy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we launched the SGUnited Jobs initiative in March.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By now, more than 16,000 immediate jobs vacancies have been made available.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is already higher than our initial target of 10,000 jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This initiative has helped jobseekers like Wendy who had a steady job as a flight attendant.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When she was placed on furlough, her friends encouraged her to check out the SGUnited Jobs Virtual Career Fair.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: She now works as a part-time cashier at Prime Supermarket while waiting for the aviation industry to recover.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In sectors that are still hiring, for example, security, WSG will ramp up the capacity of Professional Conversion Programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is for new hires aged 40 and above hired through an eligible reskilling programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I share the concerns of Mayor Denise Phua, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Rahayu Mahzam regarding fresh graduates from local and overseas institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we launched the SGUnited Traineeships Programme to help them gain industry experience, build up their resumes and boost their chances of securing jobs in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We hope more host companies can come forward to help build up the pool of traineeships and give our young graduates the much-needed opportunities to start their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Graduates can apply for these opportunities from 1 June onwards.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the strong budgetary support provided by MOF, we are holding the line on the economic front.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We recognise the many efforts by businesses and workers to adjust to the new situation as it evolves, and help one another weather the storm.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As much as we can, MOM will continue to work with our sister agencies to support businesses and protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This has been one of the most unusual periods for MOM.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We work mainly in the economic and social spheres.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workplace safety and health have always been high on our agenda.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Early in the outbreak, MOM was mobilised to help prevent imported cases.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Progressively, we limited the return of work pass holders coming through mainland China, South Korea, Iran, Italy and then worldwide.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To keep the community safe, MOH introduced the requirement for returning persons to serve a 14-day Leave of Absence, which was later tightened to be a Stay-Home Notice (SHN).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the help of GovTech, we developed in double-quick time a system of monitoring and enforcement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The system was later adapted for Singaporeans returning from abroad, to protect their families.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore was largely able to curb imported cases due to the combined efforts of many agencies on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Then, in mid-March, Malaysia announced that they would implement the Movement Control Order (MCO).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This came as a surprise to businesses who had workers commuting daily across the border.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overnight, MOM worked with MND, HDB, MTI, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) as well as community groups to source for suitable accommodation to help these businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most of the affected Malaysians have settled into new accommodation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About one in 10 subsequently returned to Malaysia, especially when Singapore introduced the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Throughout this period, migrant workers were also on our radar.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A day after the first confirmed case in Singapore, MOM reached out to dormitory operators to be more vigilant and to step up hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, one of the earliest media conferences that Minister Lawrence Wong and I held was in Tuas View Dormitory, after we inspected their quarantine facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We produced materials in the workers' native languages to encourage them to take steps to protect themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Subsequently, non-essential facilities in the dormitories like gyms and TV rooms were closed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM officers also fanned out on weekends to advise migrant workers to observe safe distancing measures and disperse big groups that were gathering at popular hangouts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The most prominent cluster of infected migrant workers was from Seletar Aerospace Heights, which was detected in February.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It involved five workers, all staying at five different locations, only two of which were dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thereafter, there was no indication of higher prevalence of COVID-19 amongst the migrant workers, compared to the general community.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Like Mr Ang Wei Neng and Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, we are very keen to understand how the virus later spread among migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Within the dormitories that have clusters, not all blocks or rooms are equally affected.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Across different dormitories, infected workers were linked through common work sites.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At work sites, it was not uncommon for the infected workers to take breaks together, share food and utensils.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, infected workers from different dormitories had gathered during their rest days to socialise and shop, for example, at Mustafa.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Back in the dormitories, workers spent time with their friends, cooking, eating and relaxing together.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The virus may have spread through all of these activities, much like how it spread among family members, religious groups and even colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One recent finding is that most of the infected workers have mild symptoms, likely because they tend to be young.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When asked if they are unwell, even after testing positive, some workers say they feel fine.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many were uncovered only because of active case-finding or swab exercises.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This may explain why, up to the middle of March, the cases of workers at the dormitories testing positive were few and far between.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Once evidence emerged that the virus had spread in the dormitories, we decided to deal with it squarely and quickly and mobilised the whole-of-Government resources.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An Inter-agency Task Force was set up, comprising officers from MOM, SAF, Home Team, MOH, MCI, MND – many agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Every day, we are joined by thousands of volunteers, especially those from the Migrant Workers' Centre.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Multiple channels of transmission among migrant workers, as appear to be the case, also means that we have to deploy a multi-faceted approach to dealing with the outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A focus on rooming arrangements on their own may not prevent a recurrence.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This consideration underpins the comprehensive approach of the Task Force.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About three weeks ago, I explained their three-pronged strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, contain the spread of the virus in the dormitories where clusters have formed; second, prevent spread in those with no clusters; and third, move out and test all workers who are still needed for essential work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I had also explained the three key enablers to implement these strategies effectively: (a) the Forward Assurance Support Teams (FAST); (b) a medical support plan that is holistic; and (c) roping in dormitory operators and employers to improve hygiene and provide necessities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The task force has gone about its work professionally, with a clear focus on the workers' well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the first phase, it was about getting the basics right.
